summary: Adds a Flask search endpoint and a Stripe config module. It also changes items pagination, downgrades lodash, loosens the Dockerfile and deploy script, and adds a CI step that echoes the PR title.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.description: The search_items handler puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string. Any caller of /search can inject SQL and read or change every table in items.db. Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a placeholder.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))
findings.problem: The search_items handler puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /search can inject SQL and read or change every table in items.db.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a placeholder.

findings.title: Pagination offset skips the first page
findings.description: The list_items handler now computes offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0. Clients never see the first 20 items, and every page shows the rows meant for the next page. Restore the offset to page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.
findings.problem: The list_items handler now computes offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0.
findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items, and every page shows the rows meant for the next page.
findings.fix: Restore the offset to page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.

findings.title: Stripe API key committed to source
findings.description: The config module hardcodes a value that matches the Stripe API key format. Anyone with repository access can use the key against the shop's Stripe account. The key stays in git history. Revoke the key and load it from an environment variable or a secret store.
findings.problem: The config module hardcodes a value that matches the Stripe API key format.
findings.consequence: Anyone with repository access can use the key against the shop's Stripe account. The key stays in git history.
findings.fix: Revoke the key and load it from an environment variable or a secret store.

findings.title: lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.description: The change pins lodash back from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. Version 4.17.15 has known prototype pollution, command injection and ReDoS flaws. Front-end code that uses lodash on untrusted data becomes exploitable again. Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in both package.json and package-lock.json.
findings.problem: The change pins lodash back from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. Version 4.17.15 has known prototype pollution, command injection and ReDoS flaws.
findings.consequence: Front-end code that uses lodash on untrusted data becomes exploitable again.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in both package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.description: The change removed the app user and the USER 10001 line. The Flask server now runs as root inside the container. Any code execution bug in the app, such as the search injection, gets root inside the container. Restore the useradd step and the USER 10001 line before CMD.
findings.problem: The change removed the app user and the USER 10001 line. The Flask server now runs as root inside the container.
findings.consequence: Any code execution bug in the app, such as the search injection, gets root inside the container.
findings.fix: Restore the useradd step and the USER 10001 line before CMD.

findings.title: Base image no longer pinned
findings.description: The change replaces the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest. Builds pick up a new Python major version without warning. The image also grows much larger. Pin the base image to a specific release tag again.
findings.problem: The change replaces the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest.
findings.consequence: Builds pick up a new Python major version without warning. The image also grows much larger.
findings.fix: Pin the base image to a specific release tag again.

findings.title: PR title expanded inside a shell step
findings.description: The workflow step puts the pull request title directly into the shell script text. A PR author can run arbitrary commands on the runner through a crafted title. The token is read-only, which limits the damage. Pass the title through an env variable and echo the quoted variable.
findings.problem: The workflow step puts the pull request title directly into the shell script text.
findings.consequence: A PR author can run arbitrary commands on the runner through a crafted title. The token is read-only, which limits the damage.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env variable and echo the quoted variable.

findings.title: Unquoted deploy directory in rm -rf
findings.description: The deploy script now passes DEPLOY_DIR to rm -rf without quotes. The shell splits a path with spaces into separate arguments. A DEPLOY_DIR with spaces makes the script delete the wrong directories. Quote the variable and keep the non-empty guard.
findings.problem: The deploy script now passes DEPLOY_DIR to rm -rf without quotes. The shell splits a path with spaces into separate arguments.
findings.consequence: A DEPLOY_DIR with spaces makes the script delete the wrong directories.
findings.fix: Quote the variable and keep the non-empty guard.

findings.title: Deploy loop parses ls output
findings.description: The loop now iterates over unquoted ls output instead of a glob. It prints bare names instead of full paths and splits names with spaces. The deploy log shows wrong or broken entries for files with spaces. Restore the quoted glob loop.
findings.problem: The loop now iterates over unquoted ls output instead of a glob. It prints bare names instead of full paths and splits names with spaces.
findings.consequence: The deploy log shows wrong or broken entries for files with spaces.

findings.title: New and changed endpoints have no tests
findings.description: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed pagination offset. Regressions such as the skipped first page reach users unnoticed. Add tests for /search with a quoted term and for /items page 1.
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed pagination offset.
findings.consequence: Regressions such as the skipped first page reach users unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for /search with a quoted term and for /items page 1.

candidate.message: Using variable interpolation `${{...}}` with `github` context data in a `run:` step could allow an attacker to inject their own code into the runner. This would allow them to steal secrets and code. `github` context data can have arbitrary user input and should be treated as untrusted. Instead, use an intermediate environment variable with `env:` to store the data and use the environment variable in the `run:` script. Be sure to use double-quotes the environment variable, like this: "$ENVVAR".

dropped.reason: This hit duplicates the PR title injection already raised for the same line.

candidate.message: Avoiding SQL string concatenation: untrusted input concatenated with raw SQL query can result in SQL Injection. In order to execute raw query safely, prepared statement should be used. SQLAlchemy provides TextualSQL to easily used prepared statement with named parameters. For complex SQL composition, use SQL Expression Language or Schema Definition Language. In most cases, SQLAlchemy ORM will be a better option.

dropped.reason: The code uses sqlite3 directly, not SQLAlchemy, and the injection is raised elsewhere.

candidate.message: Detected user input used to manually construct a SQL string. This is usually bad practice because manual construction could accidentally result in a SQL injection. An attacker could use a SQL injection to steal or modify contents of the database. Instead, use a parameterized query which is available by default in most database engines. Alternatively, consider using the Django object-relational mappers (ORM) instead of raw SQL queries.

dropped.reason: The app is Flask, not Django, and the same injection is already raised.
